column4: Okay, real talk. You wake up, check your phone, and a stock you like just ripped overnight. Or it tanked. Either way, something happened. News. A number. A rumor. In this lesson we crack the code on what actually moves a stock, and how hype turns into price. Let's get into it.

The thing that moves a stock fast has a name. A catalyst. A catalyst is news or an event big enough to shake the price loose. An earnings report, a new phone launch, a product that flops, a lawsuit, a surprise from the CEO. Look at the picture. A company drops its report, and the chart reacts almost instantly. Traders literally circle these dates on a calendar, because that is when the action happens. No catalyst, and a stock usually just drifts.

Here is the twist that trips everybody up. A company can post great numbers and the stock still drops. How? Expectations. Watch the two bars. The gray bar is what everyone already expected. The green bar is what actually happened. Price does not move on the result. It moves on the surprise, the gap between those two bars. Beat the expectation, the stock usually pops. Miss it, it dumps. Even a strong report can disappoint if the crowd was betting on something huge. That is exactly what people mean when they say it was already priced in.

Your turn. I give you a scenario, you call the reaction. Did the stock probably pop, dump, or barely move? Do not just react to the news, think about the surprise. Tap your answer and I will tell you why.

Now sort these. Some of these headlines are real catalysts that can move a price. Some are just noise, background chatter traders scroll right past. Tap a headline, then drop it in the right bucket. Learning to tell the two apart is a real edge.
Five quick questions. Show me you can spot what moves a stock, and what is just noise.

So that is the news cycle in a nutshell. Catalysts create the move, expectations decide the direction, and volume tells you if it is for real. Next up we get into options, where a single catalyst can turn a small move into a big swing, for better or way worse. Keep that surprise idea in your pocket. It is the whole game.
